predecessors.name: Kingdom of Bernicia
predecessors.text: Bernicia 'stretching from the Forth to the Tees' (Bernicia page)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Deira
predecessors.text: Deira, between the Humber and the Tees, under Aethelfrith's crown from about 604

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: the lands of the ealdormen of Bamburgh, north of the Tees, Cliopatria's last Northumbria shape

rulers.name: Ecgberht I
rulers.title: client king north of the Tyne

ledger.x: 612: Bernicia and Deira are one kingdom, Northumbria, under Aethelfrith.
616: Edwin expels Ceretic from Elmet.

c. 616: Edwin of Deira becomes king after Aethelfrith falls at the River Idle; the Bernician house gives way to the Deiran line. 'Afterward, Edwin became king of Deira and Bernicia'. Same state, same colour (rule 2); the…
626: Dunoting joins Northumbria on the map.

c. 627: Edwin rules 'much of eastern Mercia'. 'From about 627 onwards, Edwin was the most powerful king among the Anglo-Saxons, ruling Bernicia, Deira and much of eastern Mercia'. The page does not name Lindsey; Cliopatria's 626 shape adds exactly the Lindsey cells (northern Lincolnshire), and the Lindsey…

c. 627: Edwin holds the Isle of Man. The Edwin page lists the Isle of Man and Anglesey among the lands he ruled from about 627; no conquest date and no previous owner are given, so the counterpart is 'nobody'.
c. 627: Edwin holds Anglesey. The Edwin page lists the Isle of Man and Anglesey among his lands from about 627.
12 October 633: Edwin falls at Hatfield Chase and Anglesey and the Isle of Man leave Northumbria.
633: the Isle of Man leaves Northumbria with Edwin's fall.
633: Bernicia stands alone again.
633: Deira stands alone again under Osric ('Osric ruled Deira...
634: Oswald wins Heavenfield and Bernicia is reunited with Deira.
634: Bernicia rejoins the kingdom under Oswald, son of Aethelfrith.
638: Edinburgh falls to the Angles.
647: Rheged is absorbed.
655-656: Oswiu kills Penda at the Winwaed and takes Mercia.

c. 659: Mercia throws Oswiu off. 'Immin, Eata, and Eadberht led a revolt that installed Penda's son Wulfhere as ruler of the Mercians and drove out Oswiu's supporters', dated 'probably in late 659, but perhaps in 657'. Wulfhere 'apparently still recognised his primacy'. The Mercia dossier dates the revolt 658 from…
671: Ecgfrith defeats the Picts at the Battle of Two Rivers and the Northumbrians 'took control of Pictland for the next fourteen years'.
674: Ecgfrith repels Wulfhere and takes Lindsey.
679: Lindsey is returned to Mercia.
20 May 685: Ecgfrith is killed at Dun Nechtain and Pictland is lost.
705: Cliopatria's shape adds two cells (506 km2) at the Mercian edge around Manchester and the Peak, 2.9-1.9 W, 53.4-53.6 N.
750: Eadberht takes Kyle from the Britons of Alt Clut.
750: Cliopatria drops one cell (253 km2) on the Tyne at Newcastle, 54.99 N 1.48 W.
829: the Northumbrians submit to Ecgberht of Wessex at Dore.
830: the overlordship lapses.
867: Kyle drops out of the drawn kingdom with the Danish conquest of Deira.
21 March 867: the Danes take York and Deira is lost.

c. 900: Strathclyde takes the land beyond the Pennines. Rheged page: 'around 900, after Viking attacks weakened Northumbria, western lands beyond the Pennines came under Strathclyde, apparently without warfare', Cumbria staying under Strathclyde until the early 11th century. Of Cliopatria's shape only six cells near…
12 July 927: Ealdred of Bamburgh accepts Æthelstan's overlordship at Eamont, near Penrith, along with Constantine II of Alba, Hywel Dda and Owain of Strathclyde (or Morgan ap Owain of Gwent).
954: the vassal earldom of Bamburgh becomes part of England's Northumbria.
954: Eadred ends Northumbria.

wars.name: Battle of Chester
wars.outcome: Northumbrian victory: Aethelfrith 'defeated the Powysian army at Chester, killing King Selyf Sarffgadau'.

wars.name: Hatfield Chase and Cadwallon's invasion
wars.outcome: Edwin defeated and killed at Hatfield Chase (12 October 632/633) by Penda and Cadwallon; Bernicia and Deira separate under Eanfrith and Osric, both killed by Cadwallon; Oswald defeats Cadwallon at Heavenfield in 634 and reunites Northumbria.

wars.name: Winwaed campaign
wars.outcome: Oswiu kills Penda at the Winwaed (655, near Loidis) and holds Mercia until the revolt of 'probably late 659, but perhaps 657' installed Wulfhere.

wars.name: Northumbrian-Pictish war
wars.outcome: Ecgfrith's victory at the Battle of Two Rivers (671) puts Pictland under Northumbrian control for fourteen years; Ecgfrith is killed at Dun Nechtain on 20 May 685 and the Picts regain their independence.

wars.name: Northumbrian-Mercian war over Lindsey
wars.outcome: Ecgfrith repels Wulfhere and seizes Lindsey (674); Ælfwine is killed at the Trent (679) and Lindsey is returned to Mercia after Archbishop Theodore's intervention.

wars.name: Viking conquest of Northumbria
wars.outcome: The Great Heathen Army lands in East Anglia (865); Ivar takes York (866/867); Ælla and Osberht die on 21 March 867 and Deira is conquered; the north is left as a Norse client kingdom under Ecgberht I (867-872).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line survives for the whole life.
